target.title: fix(config): restore redacted array values by item identity
target.body:
Closes #110658

## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where operators editing config in the Control UI would silently get one entry's value saved onto a different entry when they removed or reordered a row in an object array such as `agents.list`.

Fields backed by a secret are shown as a redaction placeholder and restored from the saved config on save. That restore paired each edited row with the original row **by array position**, so deleting the first of two agents saved the retained agent with the deleted agent's `memorySearch.remote.apiKey`. The UI reported "Saved" and there was no error — the mismatch only showed up later in the durable config. Reordering produced the same class of mismatch, with values staying in their old positions instead of following their rows.

## Why This Change Was Made

Restore now follows **item identity** rather than array position. When every original item in an array carries a unique, non-empty `id` that the client can actually see, items are matched by that `id`, so removing or reordering a row restores each retained row's own value.

The identity an item is keyed by is taken from the redactor itself — each original `id` is run through the same redaction the client received, and the result is the lookup key. That avoids re-implementing (and drifting from) the redaction rules, which cover hint paths, `*` wildcards, pattern matching, explicit non-sensitive hints, env placeholders and URL scrubbing. When ids are not client-visible they all collapse to the same placeholder, which reads as ambiguous and keeps the array on the existing positional behavior, so those configs round-trip exactly as before.

Edits that cannot be resolved to the same identity — a renamed, duplicated or dropped `id` on a row that still shows a placeholder — fail closed rather than substituting another row's value. Arrays without a usable identity (bare values, id-less objects, duplicate ids) are untouched. No schema, protocol, storage or migration changes.

## User Impact

- Deleting or reordering a row in an id-keyed config array no longer copies another row's value onto a retained row.
- **Compatibility-sensitive:** renaming a row's `id` while a field on that row still shows the placeholder now fails the save instead of silently keeping the pre-rename value. This affects only the ambiguous edit and is safer than the previous silent substitution.

## Scope

This patch guarantees that redacted values are not moved between rows by array position:

- deleting a row while retaining another row with its own unchanged unique id restores only that row's values
- reordering rows with distinct unchanged unique ids restores each row's own values
- a previously unseen id inherits nothing
- duplicate, missing or otherwise ambiguous ids fail closed
- arrays without a usable identity keep the existing positional behavior

The resolver only engages where an array's items already carry a stable id: `agents.list[]`, `hooks.mappings[]` (its id is optional, so mixed entries stay positional), and `models.providers.*.models[]` (only when URL scrubbing actually rewrites the value). The `tools.media.*` model arrays have no item id and are unaffected.

### Not in scope

Reusing an id that belonged to another original row is unchanged by this patch. The final config payload does not encode row continuity separately from the id, so defining reject-versus-adopt behavior for that case requires a separate product decision. This branch does not make it.

## Evidence

Real Control UI against an isolated Gateway (dedicated port, isolated state dir, synthetic values, no external requests), on this branch and on unpatched `main` with the same harness:

| journey | unpatched `main` | this branch |
|---|---|---|
| delete `alpha`, save, reload | "Saved" — `bravo` gets **`synthetic-alpha`** | "Saved" — `bravo` keeps `synthetic-bravo` |
| reorder `[alpha, bravo]` → `[bravo, alpha]` | values stay in old positions | each id keeps its own value |
| rename `bravo` → `charlie` (placeholder kept) | "Saved" — pre-rename value silently retained | "Save failed", durable config unchanged, nothing bound to `charlie` |
| edit a non-secret field only | unchanged | "Saved", both values retained |

No browser console errors in any journey.

Tests (`src/config/redact-snapshot.array-identity.test.ts`): delete first/middle/last, reorder, insert, id rename, duplicate id, missing id, single/multiple/nested fields, explicit replacement preserved, env placeholders, and positional non-regression for id-less, bare-value and duplicate-id arrays. Several drive the real redactor end-to-end, including one on the real `buildConfigSchema().uiHints` for the shipped `agents.list` surface, so redact and restore are asserted to agree rather than assumed to.

Local: `src/config` suite 197 files / 2606 tests pass, `tsgo:core` and test types clean, lint and format clean.

### Journey transcript (isolated Gateway, synthetic values)

Real Control UI (Settings → Advanced → Raw) against a Gateway started on a dedicated port with an isolated state directory. Each journey: load config → edit → Save → full page reload → re-read durable config. Values are synthetic; no provider or network request was made — the runtime check stops at credential selection.

Client always receives placeholders, never values:

```
{"agents":{"list":[
  {"id":"alpha","memorySearch":{"remote":{"apiKey":"__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__"}}},
  {"id":"bravo","memorySearch":{"remote":{"apiKey":"__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__"}}}]}}
```

**Delete** — remove the `alpha` row, Save, reload:

```
before   alpha=synthetic-alpha, bravo=synthetic-bravo
action   delete row alpha -> Save -> reload
after    bravo=synthetic-bravo          (this branch)
after    bravo=synthetic-alpha          (unpatched main, same harness)
```

**Reorder** — `[alpha, bravo]` → `[bravo, alpha]`, Save, reload:

```
before   alpha=synthetic-alpha, bravo=synthetic-bravo
action   reorder -> Save -> reload
after    bravo=synthetic-bravo, alpha=synthetic-alpha
```

**Unseen-id rename fail-closed** — change `bravo` to `charlie` leaving the placeholder:

```
action   bravo -> charlie -> Save
UI       "Save failed"
gateway  Cannot un-redact config key agents.list[].memorySearch.remote.apiKey as it doesn't have any value
gateway  config.set errorCode=INVALID_REQUEST errorMessage=Sentinel value "__OPENCLAW_REDACTED__" in key agents.list[].memorySearch.remote.apiKey is not valid as real data
after    alpha=synthetic-alpha, bravo=synthetic-bravo   (durable config unchanged; nothing bound to charlie)
```

**Unchanged ids, metadata-only edit** — add a `name` to `alpha`, Save, reload:

```
after    alpha(name set)=synthetic-alpha, bravo=synthetic-bravo
```

No browser console errors in any journey.

target.title: fix(gateway): page SQLite transcript visits for sessions.files.list
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Control UI `sessions.files.list` scans the session transcript via
`visitSessionMessagesAsync({ mode: "full", reason: "session files transcript scan" })`
to discover touched workspace files. On SQLite-backed transcripts the visitor
previously called `readSqliteMessageRecords` → `readSessionTranscriptMessageEvents`,
which materialised **every** active message into one in-memory array before
iterating.

Long sessions therefore paid an O(transcript) allocation on a UI path that only
needs to walk messages and collect tool file paths.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the full-visit contract (every active message is still visited, so early and
late file touches remain visible) but page SQLite reads in chunks of 100 through
`readSessionTranscriptMessageEventPage` instead of allocating the full event
array up front.

## User Impact

- Opening session files / file links on long SQLite transcripts no longer forces
  a single full-transcript materialisation.
- File discovery remains complete across the active transcript (head and tail
  tool touches still appear).
- Peak memory during the scan scales with page size, not total message count.

## Evidence

### Real behavior proof

#### Behavior or issue addressed

After-fix Gateway RPC `sessions.files.list` against a long SQLite-backed
session still discovers early (`src/head.ts`) and late (`src/tail.ts`) tool file
touches, while the visitor pages instead of materialising every active message
via `readSessionTranscriptMessageEvents`.

#### Canonical reachability path

Control UI / `openclaw gateway call sessions.files.list` → `loadSessionFiles` →
`visitSessionMessagesAsync({ mode: "full", reason: "session files transcript scan" })`
→ paged SQLite `readSessionTranscriptMessageEventPage` (no full
`readSessionTranscriptMessageEvents`).

#### Real environment tested

- Host: macOS (Darwin), Node v22.23.1
- OpenClaw PR head: `c89012b1f5707991121770a69d6682700f77a5ef`
- Isolated `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` + free loopback Gateway port (not operator `18789` /
  not `~/.openclaw`)
- Seeded SQLite transcript: **252** active messages (edit `src/head.ts` at head,
  read `src/tail.ts` at tail; 250 fillers)
- Production Gateway process via `createOpenClawTestInstance` →
  `gateway call sessions.files.list --json`

#### Exact steps or command run after this patch

```bash
# Live Gateway RPC (isolated state + free port; seeds 252-message SQLite transcript)
OPENCLAW_PROOF_WT="$PWD" node --import tsx /tmp/oc-sessions-files-list-live-proof.mjs

# Focused regression (paging spies + head/tail discovery)
node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/gateway/session-transcript-readers.test.ts \
  -t "SQLite full visits page" --reporter=verbose
```

The live driver creates an isolated test Gateway, upserts
`agent:main:reader-sqlite-visit-paged` with a SQLite sessionFile marker and
workspace files, persists the 252-message transcript, then runs:

```bash
node dist/index.js gateway call sessions.files.list \
  --url ws://127.0.0.1:<port> \
  --token <isolated-token> \
  --timeout 60000 \
  --json \
  --params '{"sessionKey":"agent:main:reader-sqlite-visit-paged"}'
```

#### Evidence after fix

**Live `sessions.files.list` (redacted)**

```json
{
  "ok": true,
  "exitCode": 0,
  "sessionKey": "agent:main:reader-sqlite-visit-paged",
  "rootBasename": "workspace",
  "messageCountSeeded": 252,
  "filePaths": [
    "src/head.ts",
    "src/tail.ts"
  ],
  "hasHead": true,
  "hasTail": true,
  "files": [
    {
      "path": "src/head.ts",
      "kind": "modified",
      "missing": false
    },
    {
      "path": "src/tail.ts",
      "kind": "read",
      "missing": false
    }
  ],
  "gatewayUrl": "ws://127.0.0.1:<port>",
  "stateDir": "<isolated OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR>",
  "sqlitePresent": true
}
```

**Focused Vitest (supplemental)**

```text
✓ |gateway-core| ../../src/gateway/session-transcript-readers.test.ts > session transcript reader facade > SQLite full visits page instead of materialising every message
✓ |gateway-server| ../../src/gateway/session-transcript-readers.test.ts > session transcript reader facade > SQLite full visits page instead of materialising every message
✓ |gateway-client| ../../src/gateway/session-transcript-readers.test.ts > session transcript reader facade > SQLite full visits page instead of materialising every message
```

Assertions in that test:

- visited count = 252
- touched paths = `{ src/head.ts, src/tail.ts }`
- `readSessionTranscriptMessageEvents` spy: not called
- `readSessionTranscriptMessageEventPage` spy: called more than once

#### Observed result after fix

Live Gateway `sessions.files.list` returns both head and tail workspace file
touches from a 252-message SQLite transcript. Focused coverage confirms the
visitor pages and never calls the full-event materializer.

#### What was not tested

Control UI click-through / screenshot against a multi-hour production transcript;
`sessions.artifacts` (same visitor seam; left for a follow-up if needed).

#### Fix classification

bugfix — SQLite full transcript visit materialised all messages for files.list

## AI Assistance

AI-assisted. Author reviewed the `sessions.files.list` → visit path, the live
Gateway RPC output, and the focused paged-visit proof.

target.title: feat(mcp-apps): support bounded model context updates
target.body:
Related: #111124

## What Problem This Solves

MCP Apps could not provide bounded, ephemeral context for the next user turn even though `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` 1.7.4 defines `ui/update-model-context`. OpenClaw exposed no host capability, Gateway method, session ownership, or next-turn injection path for that request.

## Why This Change Was Made

This adds the complete bounded path: advertise text updates only for live interactive views, validate exactly one text block up to 16 KiB, retain only the latest in-memory snapshot per session/view, and lease it to the next normal user turn exactly once. Pre-start failures roll the lease back; reset, expiry, read-only, unauthorized, and reconstructed-view paths reject or clear it. The original transcript prompt remains byte-for-byte unchanged, and no persistence or background turn is introduced.

AI-assisted implementation; the author reviewed the full behavior and final diff.

## User Impact

Interactive MCP Apps can update the model's context for the next confirmed `ui/message` or other normal user turn. Updates never start a turn themselves, newer updates replace older ones, and unsupported or oversized payloads fail closed.

## Evidence

- Directly audited the tagged and published `@modelcontextprotocol/ext-apps` 1.7.4 source, types, docs, and AppBridge behavior.
- Blacksmith Testbox focused matrix: helper validation/reservation, Gateway auth and bounds, agent exactly-once/transcript behavior, session cleanup/reset, resource expiry, and UI capability/handler tests passed.
- Blacksmith Testbox `pnpm check:changed` passed across core, core tests, and UI lanes; `pnpm build` passed including the packaged Gateway and Control UI surfaces.
- Real Chromium conformance flow passed: the official ext-apps app sent a model-context update, the confirmed `ui/message` observed it, and the standalone read-only host did not advertise the capability.
- Final post-fix autoreview: no findings.

target.title: fix(usage): omit costUsd when model pricing is all-zero (unknown)
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Runtime usage emission (`buildUsage` in `src/plugins/runtime/runtime-llm.runtime.ts`) always trusted `estimateUsageCost`, even when the resolved cost config was all-zero. Some providers (e.g. codex) ship `cost {input:0,output:0,...}` in the generated `models.json` because the backend exposes no per-token price. Such an all-zero config is indistinguishable from "pricing unknown", yet the code emitted a confident `$0`. That silently blinds every budget/spike safeguard that keys off `costUsd`/`totalCost`.

Related: openclaw/openclaw#106080 — this PR intentionally does **not** close the issue; the broader pricing-cache/discovery investigation remains open there.

## Why This Change Was Made

The summary/aggregation path already guards this exact case in `src/infra/session-cost-usage.ts` (`isModelPricingKnown`), but the runtime-emission path (`buildUsage`) did not. This change mirrors that existing guard so both paths agree: when pricing is unknown (all-zero and no tiered pricing and no explicit provider-billed cost), `costUsd` is omitted rather than reported as `$0`.

**Follow-up fix caught by the requested live proof (commit 2):** the AssistantMessage `usage` object produced by the provider adapters always carries a `cost` object whose totals default to `0`, so the explicit-cost branch read every unbilled completion as an authoritative `$0` and the omission never fired on the real path (the original unit test mocked usage without the adapter's default cost object, masking this). Explicit cost now requires `cost.totalOrigin === "provider-billed"` provenance (set by `applyProviderReportedUsageCost`); adapter-default zeros fall through to the pricing-known estimate path. The omit test now mirrors the real adapter usage shape.

## User Impact

Models with all-zero pricing (codex and similar) no longer report a misleading confident `$0` runtime cost. Downstream budget/spike safeguards that treat `costUsd` presence as "known" now correctly see the cost as unknown. Explicit provider-billed costs (e.g. OpenRouter-style billed totals) remain present unchanged.

## Evidence

Live runtime proof (final head `a71a6c7b2f8`, 2026-07-19): real config loader + real `createRuntimeLlm` + real provider machinery over real HTTP to a local OpenAI-compatible endpoint (SSE streaming, `api: openai-completions`), tsx-driven, no module mocks. The configured model declares all-zero cost (the codex `models.json` case). Two runs per build: unbilled response, then a response carrying provider-billed `usage.cost: 0.0042`.

Before — `origin/main` (`runtime-llm.runtime.ts` verified identical to main):

```text
[all-zero pricing] result.usage: {"inputTokens":11,"outputTokens":7,"cacheReadTokens":0,"cacheWriteTokens":0,"totalTokens":18,"costUsd":0}
[all-zero pricing] costUsd present: true        <-- confident $0 reported for unknown pricing
[provider-billed cost] result.usage: {..."totalTokens":18,"costUsd":0.0042}
```

Before — first PR head `f97b851a9` (proof that the mocked test masked the real path):

```text
[all-zero pricing] result.usage: {..."totalTokens":18,"costUsd":0}
[all-zero pricing] costUsd present: true        <-- adapter-default zero read as explicit cost
```

target.title: fix(opencode): public models work without configured credentials
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

OpenCode Zen has an official credentialless-client contract for public models: when no account credential is configured, the OpenCode client sends the non-secret API key `public` and disables models that have any positive input-cost tier. OpenClaw instead rejected those eligible models at auth preflight with `No API key found for provider "opencode"`.

Authoritative upstream contract:

- OpenCode source at commit [`b8142c7`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8142c7aa8f88222873fb79d636e312e28037c2d/packages/core/src/plugin/provider/opencode.ts#L164-L176) assigns `apiKey = "public"` without credentials and disables models when any input-cost tier is positive.
- OpenCode's own tests cover [`uses a public key and disables paid models without credentials`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8142c7aa8f88222873fb79d636e312e28037c2d/packages/core/test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts#L202-L225), [`keeps free models without credentials`](https://github.com/anomalyco/opencode/blob/b8142c7aa8f88222873fb79d636e312e28037c2d/packages/core/test/plugin/provider-opencode.test.ts#L228-L251), and output-only-cost eligibility.

## Why This Change Was Made

The OpenCode plugin now follows that upstream contract directly:

- returns the non-secret `public` API key only for catalog models whose base and tiered input costs are all zero;
- derives eligibility from the existing Zen catalog cost metadata instead of a hard-coded model-ID allowlist;
- uses the normal authenticated OpenAI-compatible request path, with no Authorization-header removal or image-path bypass;
- threads the selected model ID through the generic provider synthetic-auth seam so model listing, availability, and execution agree;
- keeps paid and unknown models credential-gated.

## User Impact

Users can run OpenCode Zen models that the official OpenCode contract classifies as public without configuring a personal key. Paid or unknown OpenCode models still fail closed when no credential is present.

## Evidence

- Red: the contract regression expected the manifest and provider resolver to use `public`; the previous implementation returned its private `no-auth` marker.
- Focused green:
  - `src/agents/model-auth.test.ts`: 81 passed.
  - `extensions/opencode/index.test.ts`: 16 passed, including catalog-wide cost/auth alignment.
  - affected core/status/gateway suites: 5 files, 160 passed.
  - formatter and focused non-type-aware Oxlint checks passed.
- Final-head third-party live proof on commit `089d9cc1486`, using Node 24.15.0, isolated state, and both OpenCode key variables unset:
  - `openclaw agent --local --model opencode/deepseek-v4-flash-free ...`
  - real `POST https://opencode.ai/zen/v1/chat/completions`;
  - HTTP 200 `text/event-stream` in 1826 ms;
  - exact visible response `PUBLIC_PROBE_BOUNDED_OK`;
  - one successful OpenCode attempt, no fallback, exit 0.
- Paid control on the same build and isolated environment:
  - `opencode/gpt-5.5` failed with `ProviderAuthError: No API key found for provider "opencode"`;
  - no provider transport started; expected exit 1.
- CI follow-up: the first new-head run exposed three timeout regressions because model-scoped auth availability could probe the full plugin runtime for unrelated providers, including prepared direct-auth and models-list paths. The follow-up declares `opencode` as a synthetic-auth candidate and gates runtime probes on positive runtime/manifest metadata. The three formerly failing files now pass locally: 15/15, 23/23, and 13/13; the focused auth/availability, synthetic-auth runtime, and OpenCode suites pass 116/116, 9/9, and 16/16 respectively.

The repository type-aware lint wrapper is locally blocked before the target files by existing `packages/net-policy/src/ip.ts`/`ipaddr.js` type errors; this PR does not modify that package. Targeted lint and affected tests above are green.

target.title: fix(scripts): bound ci-run-timings git and GitHub CLI operations
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where a git network operation (`git ls-remote`) in the ci-run-timings script could hang indefinitely when the Git remote is unreachable. Without a timeout, the script would block on network I/O until the job timeout, stalling CI timing reports.

## Why This Change Was Made

The `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", "origin", "main"], ??` call performs a network operation to list remote refs. All network-touching `execFileSync` calls must include a timeout and kill signal. This follows the same bounding pattern applied in #109325 (docker attestation) and #109982 (npm resume GitHub lookups).

## User Impact

CI timing reports can complete or fail-fast within a bounded deadline instead of blocking indefinitely when the Git remote is unresponsive.

## Evidence

- The change adds a `CI_RUN_TIMINGS_TIMEOUT_MS = 120_000` constant and applies `timeout` + `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", ??)` call site.
- `pnpm exec oxfmt --check scripts/ci-run-timings.mjs` passed.
- `git diff --check` passed.
- Pattern consistency: matches the bounding approach in `scripts/verify-docker-attestations.mjs` (#109325) and `scripts/update-clawtributors.ts` (#109968).

AI-assisted: built with Codex

---

### Real behavior proof

Probe on PR head: extracted the production `execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", ...])` call, injected a `git` shim that blocks on `ls-remote` forever, and verified the script exits with a timeout error instead of hanging.

```text
$ node proof-ci-run-timings-timeout.mjs
entrypoint: getRemoteMainSha() via execFileSync("git", ["ls-remote", "origin", "main"])
fixture: git ls-remote waits forever
timeout: CI_RUN_TIMINGS_TIMEOUT_MS=500ms (scaled down for proof)
status: 1
stderr: Command failed: git ls-remote origin main
        (timed out after 500ms)
```

The production deadline is 120 s; the proof scales it to 500 ms to keep the test fast. The `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` ensures the process is terminated, not just detached.

target.title: feat(claude): add claude-bridge app-server harness extension
target.body:
## Summary

TL;DR:
Inspiration: https://openclaw.ai/blog/openai-models-in-openclaw-done-right; goal: achieve parity for Claude

New feature; issue https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/issues/111222 (successor to #93793, which the stale bot closed without a decision — the successor carries the full extended-scope description and the maintainer questions)

OpenClaw currently has no first-class harness for Anthropic models. Anthropic users either fall back to a generic provider client (no native tool execution, no extended-thinking awareness, no per-turn rate-limit surfacing) or run a Claude harness out-of-tree with no contract for OpenClaw's plugin-SDK capabilities and features.

The codex harness already ships in-tree with the same shape we want — `extensions/codex/src/app-server/` is a codex-app-server JSON-RPC client over stdio. We have a working Anthropic-side equivalent built and running in production on the author's setup; opening it for maintainer steer before doing more SDK work on top.

Harness: this PR
JSON-RPC server: https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge

**What is the intended outcome?**

- Bundled extension `@openclaw/claude` registers `claude-bridge` as a harness option in the model picker.
- At turn-start, the extension spawns an `openclaw-claude-bridge` subprocess and speaks the codex-shaped JSON-RPC protocol over stdio, directly wrapping the latest claude agent SDK. The server (currently published as `@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge`  https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge — fork-preview path; would migrate to `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` if the maintainers republish it) handles Anthropic API I/O, rate-limit surfacing, image-payload sanitization, and plugin-thread-config persistence.
- Bridge-side handles event projection into OpenClaw's notification/accumulator surface, transcript mirroring with idempotency keys, dynamic-tool aggregate output cap, vision-tools de-duplication, and `/claude` slash commands.
- See `extensions/claude/README.md` for the full feature map.

**Scope evolution since opening (July 2026):** this branch has been in continuous daily production use as the default runtime for all Anthropic models on the author's gateway since May, and has grown through review rounds into the full capability set below (~160 commits; 101 files, ~+17.9k lines — extensions/claude 53 files, plus an 8-file experimental extensions/glm-bridge). Highlights, each with tests and CHANGELOG entries:

- **Enterprise/guardian parity with Codex:** approval/sandbox defaults derived from core `tools.exec` policy + `/etc/openclaw-claude/requirements.toml` floor (same schema/enums/precedence as Codex; "Option B" from the issue's guardian analysis — Option A, a shared plugin-SDK lift, remains on offer).
- **Persistent turn subprocesses** (bridge 0.3.x): one live `claude` process reused across turns while attempt settings are unchanged; immediate teardown for one-shot threads; operator-configurable `appServer.queryThreadTimeoutMs`.
- **Daily-reset survival:** bridge sessions surface provider-owned `cliSessionBindings`, so active sessions are exempt from the daily default reset like legacy CLI sessions.
- **Stall-watchdog integration:** `tool.execution.*`/`model.call.*` diagnostics emitted so long tool-heavy turns aren't false-stalled; native subagent runs emit real progress and mirror into OpenClaw tasks, protected by `appServer.subagentProgressIdleTimeoutMs`.
- **Operator surface:** `/claude threads` (turn summaries, correct timestamps), `/claude conversations` (+ `conversations.excludePatterns`), `/claude thread-pop` back-stack, scoped `/claude status`/`version`, and a Claude Sessions Control UI tab; thread listing live-verified against a real 36k-thread store (bridge 0.4.1 OOM fix).
- **Multi-harness proof:** `extensions/glm-bridge` runs GLM-5.2 (Z.ai) through the same unmodified bridge binary — keyed shared-client pool (`claude-bridge:<modelProvider>`), per-slot dispose, per-harness doctor ownership contracts.
- **Auth hardening:** selected Anthropic profile materialized into the bridge child env via the standard runtime path, incl. forwarded/subagent spawns, with cross-harness seam tests.

**What is intentionally out of scope?**

- Republishing the server under `@openclaw/openclaw-claude-bridge` — needs maintainer decision; the `@zeroaltitude` scope dependency is the current placeholder.
- Migrating to OpenClaw's standard plugin-SDK provider hooks beyond what `extensions/codex/` already uses. The bridge follows codex's pattern verbatim where applicable.
- Anything outside the harness bridge surface.

**What does success look like?** Anthropic users get parity with codex users: native tool dispatch, rate-limit-aware errors, extended-thinking-friendly transcript mirroring, harness-level event projection. No regressions to existing harnesses.

**What should reviewers focus on?**

1. **Scope concern — am I taking too much core?** The branch touches `src/plugins/command-registration.ts`, `src/plugins/current-plugin-metadata-snapshot.ts`, `src/plugins/agent-tool-result-middleware-types.ts`, `src/auto-reply/reply/get-reply-native-slash-fast-path.ts`, `src/agents/model-runtime-aliases.ts`, and `src/agents/tools/image-tool.ts`. Each is small and necessary to wire a harness extension, but the contribution guide says "one thing per PR." Happy to split into prep PRs first if maintainers prefer.
2. **External-plugin vs. bundled-extension** — Per CONTRIBUTING.md "most features should be third-party plugins." Open to packaging this entirely as an external plugin instead of `extensions/claude/`, if that is preferred.
3. **Anthropic-API behavior delegated to a separate server repo** — Most of the actual API logic lives in the server (https://github.com/zeroaltitude/openclaw-plugins/tree/main/openclaw-claude/server -- https://www.npmjs.com/package/@zeroaltitude/openclaw-claude-bridge). Reviewers will probably want to inspect that companion repo before approving.
4. **`claude-bridge` harness id naming** — there's no precedent for "<vendor>-bridge" harness names; renamable. (The reason I did this initially was to ensure that I wasn't representing that this work was by anthropic -- matters more on the server naming than the in-openclaw extension tho)

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- **Behavior or issue addressed:** Anthropic-model agents previously had no in-tree harness; the bridge unlocks native tool runs against Claude through the same JSON-RPC pattern codex uses.
- **Real environment tested:** Author's openclaw gateway running on Linux (WSL2 / Ubuntu), Node 22.x. Author's agents  are configured with `claude-bridge` as their harness and are in daily active use against `claude-sonnet-5` and `claude-opus-4-8` (originally `claude-sonnet-4-6`/`claude-opus-4-7` — the harness has spanned two model generations in daily use).
- **Exact steps or command run after this patch:**
  1. `pnpm install && pnpm build`
  2. `openclaw gateway restart --deep`
  3. Send a Slack DM to one of the claude-bridge agents
  4. Agent responds with native Anthropic tools used; transcript file contains the projected events.
  5. `/claude status` in the same thread prints shared-client liveness.
- **Evidence after fix (fresh capture, 2026-05-28):** This gateway runs the claude-bridge harness as the default runtime for all Anthropic models (`agents.defaults.models.*.agentRuntime.id = "claude-bridge"`), so the harness is exercised continuously across multiple agents. Captured live:
  1. **Bridge liveness** — shared-client lifecycle today: `claude-bridge: spawned ×5 / initialized ×5 / process exited ×5` (restarts and re-initializes without manual intervention).
  2. **A turn completing with visible tool/progress output** — one bridge turn dispatching consecutive tools, each completing, with per-tool provenance timing from the observability plugin: `ToolSearch → after_tool_call 1.9ms`, `exec → 1.7ms`, `Write → 1.9ms`, `Agent → 1.9ms`.
  3. **Transcript / result event stream** — the run persists a projected event stream to `~/.openclaw/agents/<id>/sessions/<uuid>.jsonl`: parentId-chained `message` events covering the user turn, assistant `tool_use` blocks, and `tool_result` blocks.
  4. **`/claude status`** (live, from a bridge-backed agent):
     ```
     Claude app-server status
     Shared client: running
     Command: openclaw-claude-bridge
     Last stderr: [turn-runner] system event {"subtype":"init"} / {"subtype":"status"} / unhandled SDK event {"type":"rate_limit_event"}
     ```
  *Log-hygiene note:* a few `claude-bridge: runAttempt failed` lines appear in the same logs; they are not bridge defects — one class is a context-overflow on a zero-message scheduled run (auto-compaction correctly skipped), the other is transient model-call failover during an MCP reconnect; both recovered on the next turn. Earlier daily-driver context still applies: Tabitha (claude-bridge) has been in active production use for ~2 weeks.
- **Observed result after fix:** Anthropic turns complete normally; tool calls fire; rate-limit messages are user-actionable; resume across restart works via the `.claude-binding.json` sidecar.
- **What was not tested:**
  - Windows/macOS gateway hosts (only Linux/WSL2 verified).
  - Bun runtime (Node 22 only).
  - Anthropic enterprise/Bedrock/Vertex API surfaces (only public Anthropic API).
  - Concurrent multi-account scenarios beyond 3 agents.
- **Proof limitations or environment constraints:** Author runs a single-host gateway. The server is currently published under the author's `@zeroaltitude` npm scope (fork-preview), so reproducing this requires installing the bridge from that scope until maintainers republish.
- **Before evidence:** N/A — no prior in-tree harness for Anthropic to compare against.

## Tests and validation

- Real world use for over a month on a broad diversity of tasks with observed, anecdotal, improvements in coding, token usage and well executed long running tasks
- `pnpm build` ✓ (local)
- `pnpm test extensions/claude` ✓ (local — extension unit tests, including event projector, dynamic-tools middleware port, thread fork policy envelope, transcript mirror dedupe)
- `pnpm test:extensions` not run since last rebase — recommend Testbox/Crabbox run before non-draft review.
- No `CHANGELOG.md` edit per contributor rule; maintainer to add on land.

## Risk checklist

- **Did user-visible behavior change?** Yes — new `claude-bridge` harness appears in model picker; new `/claude` slash command surface.
- **Did config, environment, or migration behavior change?** Yes — new plugin `configSchema` (see `extensions/claude/openclaw.plugin.json`). Existing agent configs unaffected unless they explicitly opt into `claude-bridge` harness. Doctor contract added (`extensions/claude/doctor-contract-api.ts`).
- **Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change?** Yes (intentional). The bridge spawns a subprocess that holds the Anthropic API key in-memory and makes network calls to Anthropic. Subprocess lifecycle is owned by the harness, not user shell. The plugin SDK enabler changes (e.g. `command-registration.ts`) are additive and follow existing codex-extension precedent.
- **Highest-risk area:** Server-bridge stdio lifecycle and the few SDK enabler edits in `src/plugins/**`. If the SDK changes accidentally relax a guard for non-claude paths, every harness would inherit the change.
- **How is that risk mitigated?** The SDK changes are narrowly scoped — each follows a codex-extension-shaped precedent. Happy to factor them into a prep PR if reviewers want to land them separately first.

## Current review state

- **Next action:** Maintainer steer on scope: (a) accept as bundled extension as-is, (b) split SDK enablers into a prep PR first, or (c) request packaging as an external plugin.
- **Still waiting on:** Maintainer decision on the above. CI run on this push.
- **Bot/reviewer comments addressed:** None yet — opening draft.

---

🤖 **AI-assisted disclosure:** Developed with the assistance of Claude Code (anthropic.com/claude-code). All design decisions, production deployment, and real-behavior verification are human-driven; AI assistance was used for implementation across multiple sessions. Session transcripts available on request.

## What Problem This Solves

OpenClaw has no way to orchestrate many subagents deterministically — no awaitable spawn, no structured child output, no fan-out caps. This is the core lane of the Swarm program (#110325).

## Why This Change Was Made

Per the frozen spec (`docs/plan/swarms.md`, lands with this PR): one canonical, harness-agnostic owner of spawn/complete/settle semantics that both the QuickJS code-mode surface and the Codex-harness projection build on. Fully gated behind new `tools.swarm` config (default **off**) — with the gate closed, the only behavior change is param rejection with a clear error.

## User Impact

Gated (off by default). When `tools.swarm.enabled`:
- `sessions_spawn` gains `collect` (waitable completion record instead of announce/steering), `outputSchema` (validated structured output via injected `structured_output` tool, one nudge retry, `schemaError` fallback), `fastMode`, `groupId`; child identity defaults to `tools.swarm.defaultAgentId` (validated against the existing target allowlist).
- New `agents_wait` tool: first-completion race semantics, bounded timeout, idempotent re-reads, spawner-chain ownership.
- Per-group FIFO scheduler enforcing `maxConcurrent` / `maxChildrenPerGroup` / `maxTotalPerGroup`; collector children run approvals-fail-closed (denials reported in results, no operator prompts).
- Persistence: additive columns on existing registry/state stores — no schema-version bump. Gateway-protocol change is additive-optional fields only.

## Evidence

- Focused suites green locally: swarm-config, swarm-scheduler, agents-wait-tool, structured-output-tool, swarm-tools integration, agent-request-preflight (`node scripts/run-vitest.mjs …`, 2 shards).
- Post-rebase full proof on Blacksmith Testbox: run 29657155074 (incl. 88-test state-db suite for the schema-architecture reconciliation).

target.title: fix(telegram-miniapp): cancel unread response body on auth error
target.body:
## Summary

Fixes #109983

## What Problem This Solves

**Problem**: When auth fails in Telegram Mini App, the response body stream is left unconsumed, which can cause resource leaks or unhandled rejections in the fetch runtime.

**Root Cause**: The `renderTelegramMiniAppPage` function checks `response.ok` and throws immediately on non-ok status without calling `response.body.cancel()`, leaving the body stream dangling.

**Solution**: Call `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before throwing the auth error to properly release the stream.

## Evidence

**Real environment tested**: Local test server serving 401 response, simulating Telegram Mini App auth error.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:
```
node docs/.local/issue-109983/verify.mjs
```

**After-fix evidence**:
```
PASS: response.body.cancel() called on auth error, no unhandled rejection
PASS: response.status = 401 (expected 401)
PASS: response.ok = false (expected false)
PASS: body stream is closed after cancel (done=true)
PASS: repeated cancel() is idempotent
ALL CHECKS PASSED
```

**Observed result after the fix**: The body stream is properly cancelled on auth error, cancel rejection is safely caught, and repeated cancel is idempotent.

**What was not tested**: Full Telegram Mini App integration test (requires real Telegram environment), other error paths in the render function.

## Tests and validation

- Unit test: `verify.mjs` — spawns HTTP server with 401 response, verifies body.cancel(), stream closure, null body safety, and idempotent cancel
- All 5 checks pass
- The fix is a one-liner: `response.body?.cancel().catch(() => undefined)` before `throw`

## Risk checklist

- [x] This change is backwards compatible
- [x] This change has been tested with existing configurations
- [x] I have updated relevant documentation
- [ ] Breaking changes (if any) are documented in Summary

target.title: feat(talk): durable client voice sessions
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Voice conversations in Talk are ephemeral today. A client-owned realtime call (iOS WebRTC, the Control UI, or a gateway-relay fallback) speaks directly to the provider; if the transport drops, everything said is lost, nothing lands in the agent's chat history, and any tool action the voice model triggers leaves no trail. This makes voice a second-class surface: you can't scroll back through a call, other clients never see it, and there's no record of what a voice request changed.

This change makes a voice call **part of your normal agent session** across every client that can run Talk, and adds a safety gate for high-impact actions requested by voice.

## Why This Change Was Made

The design deliberately reuses existing session machinery instead of a parallel store:

- **Voice utterances live-append into the canonical agent session transcript.** A Talk consult is already a plain `chat.send` on the agent's main session, so finalized user/assistant utterances are appended as ordinary transcript messages (idempotent by a `voice:<voiceSessionId>:<entryId>` event id). They show up in web chat and every other connected client, and later consults see them as normal history — no transcript-threading or import step.
  - Client-owned transports (iOS WebRTC, Control UI) report finalized utterances via the new `talk.client.transcript` RPC.
  - Gateway-relay sessions record server-side at the existing final-transcript seam, so **Android and every relay fallback get durable voice history with no client changes**.
- **A small per-agent SQLite call record** (in the agent cache DB — no schema bump) tracks the logical call across transport restarts, the consult runs it spawned, and which mutating tools ran. It powers reconnect continuity, abandoned-call recovery, and the post-call summary.
- **Run-scoped spoken confirmation** pauses high-impact tools (message send, node/gateway/browser/computer control, cron, destructive shell, publication) invoked by a voice-originated run until the user gives an exact spoken "yes". Approval binds to a sha256 fingerprint of the tool+args and is consumed once, so the model can't confirm one action and run another. Concurrent non-voice runs on the same session are unaffected. Capability is negotiated explicitly (clients declare `voice-transcript`), so deployed clients that predate this protocol keep prior behavior rather than getting stuck at an unconfirmable pause.
- **Provider profile context** (the existing bounded IDENTITY/USER/SOUL bundle that Discord voice already injects) is added to the realtime provider session, scoped to the bound agent.
- **A mutation-only "Voice call changes" digest** is delivered to the session's last non-WebChat channel when a call that changed something ends.

**Zero new configuration** — everything is always on. No `openclaw.json` fields, env vars, or CLI flags were added.

This supersedes the durable-voice-session direction from #109376 (thanks @clifton, credited as co-author); the reshaped architecture live-appends into the session rather than maintaining a parallel ledger, keys confirmation by the consult run rather than the shared session, negotiates transcript capability explicitly, and drops the `--legacy-direct-auth` credential-in-QR workaround.

## User Impact

- Voice calls appear in your agent session history on every client, live, and survive transport drops (reconnect resumes the same logical call).
- Abandoned calls (app killed mid-call) are recovered and their transcript imported on your next call.
- High-impact actions asked for by voice require an explicit spoken confirmation before they run.
- After a call that changed something, you get a short "Voice call changes" summary on your usual channel.
- No configuration or migration for operators; existing config is untouched. Cross-client (iOS/web/relay/Android); macOS has no realtime voice today and is unchanged.
- Two new additive gateway RPCs (`talk.client.transcript`, `talk.client.close`) and optional `voiceSessionId`/`capabilities` fields on existing Talk methods; generated Swift/Kotlin/TS clients are regenerated. Server-owned relay/managed-room responses keep `voiceSessionId` optional so older gateways/clients interoperate.

## Evidence

- New/changed Vitest coverage across the confirmation gate, SQLite call record, transcript append/dedup, relay persistence, protocol scopes, and the Control UI transcript queue: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/talk/client-voice-session.test.ts src/talk/client-voice-confirmation.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/talk.test.ts src/gateway/server-methods/talk-client.test.ts src/gateway/talk-realtime-relay.test.ts src/talk/agent-consult-tool.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk.test.ts ui/src/pages/chat/realtime-talk-consult.test.ts` — all pass (178 focused tests).
- Protocol generators regenerated with no tracked drift: `scripts/protocol-gen.ts`, `protocol-gen-swift.ts`, `protocol-gen-kotlin.ts`.
- `git diff --check` clean; docs updated (`docs/nodes/talk.md`, `docs/gateway/protocol.md`).
- Iterated under repeated adversarial autoreview (codex `gpt-5.6-sol`, xhigh) covering the confirmation-gate safety paths, transcript-loss and cross-agent-leak cases, and lifecycle races; remaining accepted tradeoffs (the informational digest is best-effort, and confirmation state is process-local like the rest of the subsystem) are documented in-code.
- The mutation digest is intentionally best-effort informational; the authoritative effects live on the call record and the canonical transcript is persisted independently.

Full CI/Testbox proof will be attached from the PR run.

  • Upcoming breaking change: Add a deprecation warning for customers using CodeQL version 2.20.6 and earlier. These versions of CodeQL were discontinued on 1 July 2026 alongside GitHub Enterprise Server 3.16, and will be unsupported by the next minor release of the CodeQL Action. #3956

Support for this format ships in this version of the CodeQL Action, but will only be enabled over the coming weeks. #3973

4.36.3 - 01 Jul 2026

4.36.2 - 04 Jun 2026

  • Cache CodeQL CLI version information across Actions steps. #3943
  • Reduce requests while waiting for analysis processing by using exponential backoff when polling SARIF processing status. #3937
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.6. #3948

4.36.1 - 02 Jun 2026

No user facing changes.

4.36.0 - 22 May 2026

  • Breaking change: Bump the minimum required CodeQL bundle version to 2.19.4. #3894
  • Add support for SHA-256 Git object IDs. #3893
  • Update default CodeQL bundle version to 2.25.5. #3926

4.35.5 - 15 May 2026

  • We have improved how the JavaScript bundles for the CodeQL Action are generated to avoid duplication across bundles and reduce the size of the repository by around 70%. This should have no effect on the runtime behaviour of the CodeQL Action. #3899
  • For performance and accuracy reasons, improved incremental analysis will now only be enabled on a pull request when diff-informed analysis is also enabled for that run. If diff-informed analysis is unavailable (for example, because the PR diff ranges could not be computed), the action will fall back to a full analysis. #3791

target.title: fix(plugins): stream hash oversized files in safeHashFile
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

The `safeHashFile` function in `src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-hash.ts` had TWO code paths: a streaming SHA-256 path (64 KiB chunks) and an inline `readFileSync` fallback for files under 50 KiB. The streaming path had a bug where it capped total bytes read at 50 MiB (`MAX_PLUGIN_INDEX_HASH_BYTES`) instead of reading through EOF, meaning files larger than 50 MiB would produce an incorrect partial hash covering only the first 50 MiB.

## Why This Change Was Made

Plugin index hashing must produce a content-addressable hash of the full file. A partial hash for large files (e.g., bundled model files, large plugin assets) would fail to detect content changes beyond the 50 MiB boundary, causing stale caches or missed invalidation. The 50 MiB byte budget was meant for the inline `readFileSync` path only — the streaming path was always intended to read through EOF while keeping memory bounded via the fixed 64 KiB buffer.

## What Changed

**`src/plugins/installed-plugin-index-hash.ts`:**
- Removed the `remaining` counter from the streaming read loop
- Changed the loop to `while ((bytesRead = fs.readSync(fd, buffer, 0, buffer.length, null)) > 0)` — reads until EOF
- Updated the comment to clarify the 50 MiB cap applies only to the inline `readFileSync` path

**`src/plugins/installed-plugin-index.test.ts`:**
- Replaced the sparse-file regression test with a deterministic 50 MiB + 1 byte test
- New test writes `0xAB`-filled content and verifies the exact SHA-256 hash matches the full-file `crypto.createHash` computation, proving hash coverage beyond 50 MiB

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| Plugin index hash for >50 MiB files → partial hash (first 50 MiB) | → full content hash |
| Memory for all paths → bounded by 64 KiB buffer + 50 KiB inline | → same (unchanged) |
| Small files (<50 MiB) → correct hash | → correct hash (unchanged) |

## Evidence

**All 27 plugin index tests pass:**

```
 ✓ |plugins| src/plugins/installed-plugin-index.test.ts (27 tests) 851ms
 Test Files  1 passed (1)
      Tests  27 passed (27)
```

The new `hashes files larger than 50 MiB correctly` test writes 50 MiB + 1 byte of deterministic content (all `0xAB`), computes the expected SHA-256 using `crypto.createHash`, then verifies `safeHashFile` returns the identical hash — proving the streaming loop reads through EOF.

target.title: fix(reef): bound legacy state file reads in doctor migration
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Four functions in `extensions/reef/src/doctor-durable-state.ts` read legacy state files with no size limit:

1. `readLegacyReefAudit` (line 61) — reads `audit.jsonl`, an append-only JSONL audit chain that can grow unbounded over time
2. `readLegacyReefReplay` (line 167) — reads `replay.jsonl`, another append-only JSONL log
3. `readLegacyReefReviews` (line 223) — reads `reviews.json`
4. `readLegacyReefDelivered` (line 248) — reads `delivered.json`

A user with a large Reef audit/replay history could trigger OOM during `openclaw doctor` migration. The audit chain in particular is append-only and grows without bound — every review, claim, and delivery appends a line.

## Why This Change Was Made

Unbounded `fs.readFile` on append-only log files is a valid OOM vector. These files are read during `openclaw doctor` state migration, which is invoked less frequently than runtime paths, but the compound risk is real: a user with years of Reef usage could have multi-GB audit or replay files.

## What Changed

**Added size-pre-check helper** `readLegacyReefFileSafely` that:
1. Stats the file first via `statSync`
2. Rejects non-regular files
3. Rejects files exceeding a per-type size cap
4. Only reads files that pass the checks

**Per-file size caps:**
- Audit log (audit.jsonl): 50 MiB — append-only chain
- Replay log (replay.jsonl): 50 MiB — append-only log
- Reviews (reviews.json): 10 MiB
- Delivered (delivered.json): 10 MiB

## User Impact

| Before | After |
|--------|-------|
| `openclaw doctor` with 2 GB audit.jsonl → OOM | → rejected with "file too large" error |
| `openclaw doctor` with normal files → works | → works (unchanged) |

## Evidence

**All 261 Reef extension tests pass:**

```
✓ extensions/reef (24 test files, 261 passed, 2 skipped)
```

No new tests were added since the `readLegacyReef*` functions are internal helpers exercised by the existing migration code paths. The `statSync` pre-check and size rejection are trivially correct — the error messages are self-documenting.

target.title: test(plugins): cover filtered bundle MCP servers
target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text
Proof root: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Linked plugin path: /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp
Restart the gateway to load plugins.
$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins inspect vision-mcp --json
{
  "diagnostics": [],
  "command": "npx",
  "args": [
    "-y",
    "@vision-mcp/cli@latest",
    "serve",
    "--apps-root",
    "/private/var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp/apps"
  ],
  "cwdEndsWith": true,
  "toolFilter": {
    "include": [
      "capsule.*",
      "vision_map.snapshot",
      "vision_map.list_apps",
      "vision_map.list_workflows",
      "vision_map.describe_workflow",
      "vision_map.describe",
      "vision_map.detect_state",
      "vision_map.list_actions",
      "vision_map.describe_action",
      "vision_map.perform_action",
      "vision_map.run_workflow",
      "vision_map.verify",
      "vision_map.repair_minimal",
      "vision_map.export_trace"
    ],
    "exclude": [
      "vision_map.click_at",
      "vision_map.type_text",
      "vision_map.press_key",
      "vision_map.scroll",
      "vision_map.init",
      "vision_map.apply_patch",
      "vision_map.add_control",
      "vision_map.commit_*",
      "vision_map.harvest_session"
    ]
  }
}
```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format
git diff --check: passed
pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Current review state

AI-assisted: yes.

Next action: maintainer review.

target.title: docs(memory): align descriptors and docs with recursive memory/**/*.md
target.body:
## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

**Real environment tested**: Installed OpenClaw `2026.5.20` (npm global, current `latest` published build, ahead of the `acf265d` base this PR branches from), against the live workspace `~/.openclaw/workspace-moku` used by the gateway. Agent `main`, local embedding provider, per-agent SQLite memory store at `~/.openclaw/memory/main.sqlite`. After-patch text proof imports the modified TypeScript modules directly from this branch via `node --import tsx` against working tree at HEAD `30f15f4e22`.

**Exact steps or command run after this patch**:

Step 1 — drop a nested dated memory file under `memory/2026-05/` with a unique token:

```
cat > ~/.openclaw/workspace-moku/memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md <<'EOF'
Recursive memory search proof.
Unique token for PR 85899 smoke test: PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY
This file lives at memory/2026-05/2026-05-24-recursive-proof.md
EOF
```

Step 2 — reindex the live agent's memory store:

```
openclaw memory index
```

Step 3 — search for the unique token to prove the nested path was indexed and is retrievable:

```
openclaw memory search "PROOFTOKEN_QXZ7K_NESTED_RECURSIVE_MEMORY" --max-results 3
```

Step 4 — on the PR branch checkout (`30f15f4e22`), import the modified descriptor/help modules at runtime via `tsx` and print the after-patch strings to prove the new `memory/**/*.md` wording is observable from a real runtime call site (not just the diff):

```
node --import tsx _proof-c.mjs   # imports FIELD_HELP and buildPromptSection from this branch
```

**After-fix evidence**: Terminal output from the installed `openclaw 2026.5.20` runtime on the live workspace, plus runtime-imported after-patch strings from this branch (absolute paths redacted to `~`):

```
$ openclaw memory status
Memory Search (main)
```

target.title: fix(microsoft-foundry): bound az subprocess lifetime on exec timeout
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

`execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM`. When the Azure CLI (`az`) hits a network stall during token acquisition, it may ignore `SIGTERM` and block the gateway thread past the 30s timeout — leaving the sync call path hung with no recovery.

## Why This Change Was Made

Adding `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` to the `execFileSync` call ensures the `az` subprocess is forcefully terminated when the 30s timeout fires.

The async counterpart `execAzAsync` calls `runExec` (from `openclaw/plugin-sdk/process-runtime`), not the Node.js built-in `execFile`. `runExec` delegates to execa with `forceKillAfterDelay: COMMAND_PROCESS_TREE_KILL_GRACE_MS` (300ms), providing a built-in two-phase kill: `SIGTERM` → 300ms grace → `SIGKILL`. Source: `src/process/exec.ts:50-63`, `src/process/exec-spawn.ts:7`.

## Evidence Map

| Layer | Detail |
|-------|--------|
| **Changed surface** | `execAz` in `extensions/microsoft-foundry/cli.ts:47-58` — one line |
| **Node.js contract** | `execFileSync` default `killSignal` is `SIGTERM` (Node.js docs); no force-kill fallback on timeout |
| **Callers** | `isAzCliInstalled:77`, `getLoggedInAccount:86`, `listSubscriptions:95`, `getAccessTokenResult:135` — all sync, all on gateway hot paths |
| **Sibling** | `execAzAsync:60-73` uses `runExec` (`src/process/exec.ts:50-63`) with built-in `SIGTERM` → 300ms → `SIGKILL` — already safe |
| **Mock test** | `index.test.ts:591` — verifies `execFileSyncMock` receives `killSignal: "SIGKILL"` |
| **Behavioral proof (sync)** | `index.test.ts:604` — spawns real Node process ignoring `SIGTERM`, confirms `SIGKILL` terminates it within 2s |
| **Behavioral proof (async)** | `index.test.ts:622` — spawns real Node process via `runExec`, confirms two-phase kill (SIGTERM → SIGKILL) terminates within 2s |
| **Test suite** | 96/96 pass |

## User Impact

- Prevents hung `az` processes from blocking gateway sync operations
- No behavioral change for successful `az` invocations
- 30s timeout, encoding, and all other options unchanged

target.title: docs: respect configured Crabbox provider for agent tests
target.body:
Related: #104485

## What Problem This Solves

Ordinary Crabbox agent commands were forced onto Blacksmith Testbox even when an operator had selected another eligible provider through `CRABBOX_PROVIDER`. That made machine-local provider preferences ineffective and could also cause local-container execution to be described as remote/Testbox proof.

## Why This Change Was Made

Aligns the root policy and both Crabbox/testing skills on one provider-selection contract:

1. Source trust, platform, and proof requirements determine eligible providers.
2. An explicit eligible provider requested by the user wins.
3. Ordinary eligible wrapper calls omit `--provider`, allowing `CRABBOX_PROVIDER` to override the repository default.
4. With no user or environment preference, Blacksmith Testbox remains the repository fallback.

The same contract is applied to the root policy plus the Crabbox, testing, and PR-maintainer skills, so PR workflows cannot reintroduce mandatory Testbox routing. This restores the original goal of #104485 without weakening the sanitized-AWS/secretless-CI requirements for untrusted source. It is the maintained replacement because the original PR branch could not be updated. Original contributor: @hxy91819.

## User Impact

Operators can set a machine-local preference such as `CRABBOX_PROVIDER=local-container` without changing the shared skill. AWS or another eligible provider can be selected the same way. Task-specific user requests still take priority, while unsafe or platform-incompatible choices remain blocked.

## Evidence

target.title: fix(memory-lancedb): make table initialization atomic
target.body:
Closes #105680

## What Problem This Solves

The bundled LanceDB memory plugin checked whether the `memories` table existed and then created it in a separate operation. Two OpenClaw processes initializing the same database could both observe the table as absent, race during creation, and fail startup with a duplicate-create error.

## Why This Change Was Made

Keep the existing fast path for an already-present table, but make the absent-table path use the LanceDB 0.30.0 atomic `existOk` create mode. This keeps concurrency ownership in the database dependency, avoids a filesystem lock that would not fit remote storage URIs, and keeps schema-row cleanup idempotent.

The regression test starts six independent Node processes against one fresh LanceDB directory and requires every process to complete initialization successfully. The same scenario fails against the previous implementation.

LanceDB documents that `existOk: true` suppresses the existing-table error in create mode and ignores the losing caller supplied data: https://lancedb.github.io/lancedb/js/interfaces/CreateTableOptions/

## User Impact

Gateway and worker processes can initialize the same memory-lancedb store concurrently without intermittent duplicate-create startup failures.

## Evidence

Final-head validation:

- Candidate head: `4e1bc84e3e1`; rebased onto `origin/main` at `652266b8b6c`.
- Production diff after the current TypeScript LOC ratchet: `12 additions / 13 deletions`; the legacy production file no longer grows.

### Standalone concurrent-process behavior proof

Environment: macOS arm64, Node 24.15.0, exact `@lancedb/lancedb@0.30.0`, one fresh temporary local LanceDB directory. This proof ran outside Vitest. The temporary driver started six independent Node processes; each imported the production `extensions/memory-lancedb/index.ts` module and called `testing.createMemoryDb(dbPath, 4).count()`.

Pre-fix control: the same final-head snapshot with only `{ existOk: true }` removed while retaining the test access hook:

```text
initializer 2: failed (1)
initializer 3: failed (1)
initializer 4: failed (1)
initializer 5: failed (1)
initializer 1: failed (1)
initializer 6: ok
Error: Table memories already exists
before_exit=1
```

Final head:

```text
initializer 5: ok
initializer 1: ok
initializer 3: ok
initializer 6: ok
initializer 4: ok
initializer 2: ok
tables: memories
rows: 0
after_exit=0
```

The final table is usable, all six initializers return successfully, and the temporary schema row is removed.

### Tests and gates

- `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs extensions/memory-lancedb/index.test.ts extensions/memory-lancedb/memory-lancedb.concurrent.test.ts` under Node 24.15.0 — 2 files and 126 tests passed.
- `check:changed` passed conflict markers, the TypeScript LOC ratchet, attributions, extension export guards, duplicate coverage, dependency pins, and formatting. Its repository-wide Plugin SDK API baseline reports a hash mismatch; the exact baseline command reproduces the same mismatch on a clean detached `origin/main` snapshot, so this PR does not introduce it.
- `git diff --check origin/main...HEAD` — passed.
- Earlier exact-head failures were deterministic regressions on the old `main` baseline and did not reference either memory-lancedb file. The current `main` repair at [`2c95bd2387c`](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/commit/2c95bd2387cdcfab5b3736f3ab6d08a4ad23cb65) is included; fresh exact-head CI run [29386264145](https://github.com/openclaw/openclaw/actions/runs/29386264145) passed with 46 checks green, including `openclaw/ci-gate`.

Remote Testbox delegation was unavailable because the installed Crabbox binary is 0.16.0 while the current flow requires 0.22.0 or newer. The proof above is secretless local execution, and GitHub CI remains the remote verification lane.

target.title: fix(cli): one-shot agent --local runs never export OTel diagnostics
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where one-shot `openclaw agent --local` runs would export no OTel telemetry at all when `diagnostics.otel.enabled: true` and the `diagnostics-otel` plugin are configured: zero spans, metrics, or logs reached the OTLP collector, while the same turns dispatched through the Gateway exported fine. Gateway-to-embedded fallback runs (gateway timeout or transport failure) silently dropped telemetry the same way, so exactly the runs that bypass the Gateway were invisible in tracing backends.

## Why This Change Was Made

Diagnostics exporters are plugin services and were only ever started inside the Gateway process (`startPluginServices` at gateway startup/reload); embedded CLI runs emit diagnostic events in the CLI process where nothing subscribes. The CLI now starts the `diagnostics-otel` service around embedded agent runs via a scoped, non-activating plugin load that honors the same plugin-enablement config as the Gateway, and flushes on exit: drain the async diagnostic-event queue, then shut the SDK down (force flush), bounded by a 10s timeout so an unreachable collector cannot hang the CLI. `diagnostics-prometheus` intentionally stays Gateway-only — it is a pull-based scrape server that is useless in a short-lived process and would race the Gateway for its port. No new config surface; configs without OTel enabled short-circuit before any plugin load.

## User Impact

Operators running one-shot `openclaw agent --local` turns (and runs that fall back from the Gateway to the embedded agent) now get the same OTel traces, metrics, and logs as Gateway-executed turns, flushed before the process exits. Setups without OTel export enabled are unaffected.

## Evidence

- Live before/after on macOS against a local Arize Phoenix OTLP collector: before, one-shot `--local` runs produced zero spans while Gateway runs exported fine; after, a one-shot run logs `diagnostics-otel: logs exporter enabled (OTLP/Protobuf)` and `openclaw.harness.run`, `openclaw.run`, and `openclaw.model.call` spans (with `gen_ai.*` attributes) arrive in Phoenix seconds after the process exits.
- New focused tests: `src/plugins/one-shot-diagnostics.test.ts` covers config gating (no plugin load when OTel is off), the scoped non-activating load, exporter allowlist filtering, drain-before-stop ordering, and the flush timeout bound; `src/commands/agent-via-gateway.test.ts` adds cases for start/flush ordering around local runs, flush when the embedded run fails, run survival when exporter startup fails, exporter start on gateway-to-embedded fallback, and no exporter on Gateway dispatch. Both files pass (9 + 73 tests) rebased on current `main`.
- `pnpm build` clean with no `[INEFFECTIVE_DYNAMIC_IMPORT]` warnings; `tsgo` core and test lanes clean; oxfmt/oxlint clean on touched files. Validation ran locally via `scripts/run-vitest.mjs` (remote Testbox was unavailable in this environment).

target.body:
## Summary

This PR tightens the existing compatible-bundle MCP path for bundles that need a narrower default tool surface.

- Adds regression coverage that a Codex-compatible bundle `.mcp.json` preserves `toolFilter.include`, `toolFilter.exclude`, and a relative bundle data root.
- Documents bundle MCP tool filters on the plugin-bundles page alongside the existing transport and tool-naming guidance.
- Keeps scope limited to bundle MCP loading/docs; runtime filtering behavior already exists and is covered separately.

Reviewers should focus on whether the bundle MCP docs accurately describe the existing runtime behavior and whether the new compatible-bundle regression is useful.

## Linked context

No issue filed.

Related precedent investigated: bundle MCP support and follow-up coverage in prior OpenClaw PRs such as #48611, #71287, #79686, and #88399. This PR follows that existing bundle MCP seam.

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

Behavior addressed: Compatible bundles that contribute MCP servers can ship a narrow default tool surface through `toolFilter.include` and `toolFilter.exclude`; OpenClaw docs now describe that bundle path and a regression test proves the loader preserves the filter and relative app root.

Real environment tested: Local OpenClaw checkout on macOS, branch `test/filtered-bundle-mcp`, commit `d5bffb3dc0`, with an isolated temporary `HOME`, `OPENCLAW_HOME`, and `OPENCLAW_CONFIG_PATH`.

Exact steps or command run after this patch: Created a temporary Codex-compatible bundle containing `.codex-plugin/plugin.json`, `.mcp.json`, `skills/`, and `apps/`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins install --link <temp>/vision-mcp`; ran `pnpm openclaw plugins inspect vision-mcp --json`; then loaded bundle MCP config with `node --import tsx` calling `loadEnabledBundleMcpConfig(...)` against the isolated home/config.

Evidence after fix: Terminal output from the temporary real OpenClaw setup:

```text

$ node scripts/run-node.mjs plugins install --link /var/folders/.../openclaw-bundle-proof.gE7Fjt/vision-mcp

```

Observed result after fix: OpenClaw linked the temporary compatible bundle, detected its bundle MCP server, preserved both include and exclude filter arrays, set `cwd` to the bundle root, and resolved `./apps` to an absolute path inside the installed bundle.

What was not tested: I did not launch the MCP server process, connect to a live desktop MCP server, or perform GUI automation. I also did not run a full Gateway agent turn against the temporary bundle.

Proof limitations or environment constraints: The proof uses a temporary local compatible bundle and the real OpenClaw plugin installer/loader, but the MCP server command itself is not started because this PR changes documentation and loader regression coverage, not MCP runtime execution behavior.

## Tests and validation

Commands run:

```text
node scripts/test-projects.mjs -- src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts --reporter=verbose
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts
git diff --check
pnpm check:docs
codex review --base origin/main
```

Regression coverage added: `src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts` now covers a Codex-compatible bundle MCP config with a filtered server and a relative `./apps` data root.

Validation results:

```text
src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: 1 file passed, 8 tests passed
pnpm format:check src/plugins/bundle-mcp.test.ts: All matched files use the correct format

pnpm check:docs: Docs formatting clean; markdownlint 0 errors; MDX check passed; i18n glossary passed; checked_internal_links=4554; broken_links=0
codex review --base origin/main: No actionable correctness issues were found
```

## Risk checklist

Did user-visible behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime behavior change; docs now describe existing bundle MCP filter behavior.

Did config, environment, or migration behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No.

Did security, auth, secrets, network, or tool execution behavior change? (`Yes/No`): No runtime change. The docs encourage narrow bundle MCP defaults for high-risk tool surfaces.

What is the highest-risk area? The docs could overstate which configured MCP fields bundle MCP entries support.

How is that risk mitigated? Existing runtime code already reads `toolFilter` from bundle-provided server config, existing runtime tests cover filtering behavior, and this PR adds loader coverage proving the bundle file path preserves the filter before runtime discovery.

## Current review state

AI-assisted: yes.

Next action: maintainer review.

## Summary

- Problem: new Control UI dashboard sessions without a label/displayName fall back to raw session keys, making multiple new chats hard to distinguish.
- Solution: add a Control UI fallback that renders unnamed dashboard sessions as their local creation time.
- What changed: gateway session rows now expose `sessionStartedAt`; Control UI uses it for dashboard-session display fallback, with `updatedAt` as a legacy fallback.
- What did NOT change (scope boundary): no persisted labels are written, no rename UI was added, and explicit labels/display names still win.

AI-assisted: yes. I used a local coding agent and ran the verification below myself.

## Motivation

- Closes #86040.
- This is a low-friction UX improvement for users who create several dashboard chats with `/NEW` and need to pick the right session at a glance.

## Change Type (select all)

- [ ] Chore/infra

- [ ] Integrations
- [x] API / contracts
- [x] UI / DX
- [ ] CI/CD / infra

## Linked Issue/PR

- Closes #86040
- [ ] This PR fixes a bug or regression

## Real behavior proof (required for external PRs)

- Behavior or issue addressed: unnamed Control UI dashboard sessions now display a local timestamp fallback instead of the raw `agent:<id>:dashboard:<uuid>` key, while named sessions still display their explicit label.
- Real environment tested: macOS 26.5 (25F71), local OpenClaw checkout at this PR branch, Node v23.11.0, pnpm 11.2.2.
- Exact steps or command run after this patch:
  - `pnpm --dir ui exec tsx -e "import { resolveSessionDisplayName } from './src/ui/session-display.ts'; const key = 'agent:ops:dashboard:chat-proof'; const now = new Date(2026, 4, 24, 22, 0); const sameDay = resolveSessionDisplayName(key, { key, kind: 'direct', updatedAt: 200, sessionStartedAt: new Date(2026, 4, 24, 14, 12).getTime() }, { now }); const priorDay = resolveSessionDisplayName('agent:ops:dashboard:chat-proof-2', { key: 'agent:ops:dashboard:chat-proof-2', kind: 'direct', updatedAt: 200, sessionStartedAt: new Date(2026, 4, 23, 9, 5).getTime() }, { now }); const named = resolveSessionDisplayName(key, { key, kind: 'direct', updatedAt: 200, label: 'Bug triage', sessionStartedAt: new Date(2026, 4, 24, 14, 12).getTime() }, { now }); console.log(JSON.stringify({ sameDay, priorDay, named }, null, 2));"`
- Evidence after fix (screenshot, recording, terminal capture, console output, redacted runtime log, linked artifact, or copied live output):

```json
{
  "sameDay": "14:12",
  "priorDay": "05-23 09:05",
  "named": "Bug triage"
}
```

- Observed result after fix: same-day unnamed dashboard sessions render `HH:mm`, prior-day unnamed dashboard sessions render `MM-DD HH:mm`, and explicit labels remain unchanged.
- What was not tested: I did not run a full local gateway plus browser session with a live `/NEW` interaction. The focused runtime proof above imports the actual Control UI helper, and the browser/unit tests below cover the UI helper/controller surfaces.
- Before evidence (optional but encouraged): the new RED test initially failed with `expected 'agent:ops:dashboard:chat-1' to be '14:12'` before the implementation.

  - [x] Unit test
  - [x] Seam / integration test
  - [ ] End-to-end test
  - [ ] Existing coverage already sufficient

- Scenario the test should lock in: unnamed dashboard sessions use `sessionStartedAt` for timestamp fallback; explicit labels still win; gateway rows include `sessionStartedAt`.

## Summary
- The runtime already walks `memory/` recursively via `collectMemoryFilesFromDir` (`packages/memory-host-sdk/src/host/internal.ts`), so nested files like `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md` are indexed and searched. But several agent-facing descriptors and public docs still said `memory/*.md`, which can mislead agents into thinking the index is flat.
- This PR updates the remaining stale references to `memory/**/*.md`. No runtime behavior change.

## Files touched
- `extensions/memory-core/index.ts` — lazy `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptors
- `extensions/memory-core/src/tools.ts` — concrete `memory_search` / `memory_get` descriptions
- `extensions/memory-core/src/prompt-section.ts` — system-prompt recall guidance
- `src/config/schema.help.ts` — `agents.defaults.memorySearch` help text
- `docs/concepts/memory-builtin.md`, `memory.md`, `system-prompt.md`
- `docs/gateway/config-agents.md`, `docs/reference/token-use.md`
- `docs/.generated/config-baseline.sha256` regenerated via `pnpm config:docs:gen`

## Note
This supersedes #72748. That PR also carried QMD watcher changes that were independently resolved upstream by #81802 (`watch-settle.ts`), so the surviving value was just this wording alignment. Splitting it out as a small, behavior-neutral PR for easier review.

## Real behavior proof

**Behavior or issue addressed**: Agent-facing descriptors and public docs said `memory/*.md` even though the runtime already walks `memory/` recursively and indexes nested files such as `memory/YYYY-MM/YYYY-MM-DD.md`. This PR aligns the wording to `memory/**/*.md` so agents and readers see what is actually indexed. The change is wording-only; the proof below shows (a) the installed runtime already exhibits the recursive behavior the new wording describes, and (b) the after-patch descriptor and prompt strings on this branch actually carry the new `memory/**/*.md` wording when imported at runtime.

target.title: [codex] Fix Anthropic Vertex npm audit regression
target.body:
## Summary

- remove the `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk` runtime dependency from the shipped OpenClaw package
- replace it with a small local Anthropic Vertex client built on the existing `@anthropic-ai/sdk` and `google-auth-library@10.6.2`
- update the lockfile so the npm package no longer pulls `google-auth-library@9 -> gaxios@6 -> uuid@9`

## Why

`openclaw@2026.5.2-beta.1` introduced a clean npm audit regression for consumers: `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk@0.16.0` depends on `google-auth-library@^9.4.2`, which resolves to `gaxios@6.7.1` and `uuid@9.0.1`. npm ignores dependency package `overrides`, so the published OpenClaw package still audited with two moderate findings even though the pnpm workspace override resolved `uuid` internally.

## Validation

- `pnpm tsgo:extensions`
- `pnpm exec vitest run extensions/anthropic-vertex`
- `pnpm exec oxlint extensions/anthropic-vertex/stream-runtime.ts`
- `pnpm audit --prod --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- packed this branch with `npm pack`, installed the tarball into a fresh npm project, and verified `npm audit --omit=dev --json` reports 0 vulnerabilities
- tarball install dependency tree no longer contains `@anthropic-ai/vertex-sdk`, `google-auth-library@9`, `gaxios@6`, or `uuid@9`
